thread:
oliver (ux): Hey team — quick sketch of a new timeline scrubber for the latency dashboard. Trying a couple of ideas: snap-to-bucket "snaplines", and a sampling-rate slider with a compact label. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.internal/tmp/scrubber-v3.png :eyes:

maria (product): Nice. Can we keep the default sampling at 100% for new users? worried about surprising cost regressions when they toggle it down.

jamal (eng): Agree on default 100%. Also: if sampling < 10% we should disable live KV-caching previews or show a warning. Sampling affects cache hit patterns. (reacts :warning:)

samira (research): From evals I've seen, p95 shifts non-linearly once < 20% sampling. Could we add a tiny inline stat next to the slider that says "expected p95 bias: +X ms" based on current selection?

oliver (ux): Good call. Mockup shows a micro-label: "est p95 delta: +12ms @ 25%". I can wire that to the backend estimate later. Thoughts on the snaplines?

maria (product): Snaplines look helpful for spotting bucket boundaries (peak/idle). But the hover target is small — maybe increase the hit area by 8px. Also copy tweak: change "Sampling rate" -> "Trace sampling"? More specific.

jamal (eng): "Trace sampling" may confuse folks who only think in request sampling. How about "Request sampling (controls trace subset)" as hover tooltip?

samira (research): Accessibility: the snapline color contrast is low on our light theme. Also keyboard support: can you arrow between snaplines and press Enter to snap? Screen reader should announce "snapline at 14:00, peak traffic".

oliver (ux): Good a11y notes. Plan: bump contrast, add focus ring, allow keyboard left/right to cycle snaplines and Enter to snap. For SR we can add aria-label with time + short reason.

jamal (eng): On implementation: continuous dragging will spam the backend. We should debounce the scrubber events client-side and send an immediate sample only when snapping or releasing. Pseudocode: ```js
let debounceTimer;
scrubber.on('drag', e => {
  clearTimeout(debounceTimer);
  debounceTimer = setTimeout(() => fetchSamples(e.time), 150);
});
// send immediate when snap or mouseup
scrubber.on('snap mouseup', e => fetchSamples(e.time));
```

maria (product): UX copy: in the panel header replace "Sampling" with "Sampling controls" and add a question-mark tooltip: "Lower sampling reduces cost but may hide rare latency spikes." Short and friendly.

samira (research): Metrics to show: selection size, effective throughput estimate, and an "estimated detection power" for anomalies. Those help PMs choose a sampling point.

oliver (ux): I like "estimated detection power" — short label: "Detection power". Will place as micro-metric under slider. Also proposing a compact toggle: "Auto-suggest sampling" which proposes a value based on traffic and cost targets.

jamal (eng): Auto-suggest needs a safety cap per org: min 1% unless OrgOpt-in to 0.5%. Also include a rollout flag.

maria (product): For onboarding, default card should show "Why sampling matters" with a one-liner + link to docs. Also include a link to run a quick simulation: "Simulate how sampling affects p95".

oliver (ux): Next steps: I'll update mock with bigger hit targets, higher contrast, detection-power micro-stat, and the auto-suggest toggle. Will push an updated prototype later today. Any last items?

designbot: Checklist: 1) keyboard nav added, 2) contrast >= 4.5:1, 3) debounce 150ms, 4) default sampling 100%, 5) tooltip copy approved. Marking in taskboard.

maria (product): Thanks — please ping when prototype is up, I'll gather PM feedback and check docs blurb. :thumbsup:

jamal (eng): I'll add the debounce + snap events to the runtime SDK branch and include a feature flag.

samira (research): I'll prepare a quick eval run to estimate detection-power numbers for the slider defaults.

oliver (ux): Great — closing loop. Will post the updated prototype here (link + short video) in ~2h. (reacts :sparkles:)
